chain: Pope Francis succeeded Pope John Paul II. (edit)
'Succeeded as pope' is the inverse of 'preceded as pope', so John Paul II preceded Francis as pope: Francis is the pope who came after him.
'Preceded as pope' is functional (a pope has one immediate successor), so the stored 'Benedict XVI succeeded John Paul II' cannot also hold; the answer is Pope Francis.

notes: Dev-split ABox revision on succeeded_as_pope (new relation, staging/people.RELATIONS.md: functional, inverse of preceded_as_pope, which is also functional); the edit carries the inverse property of the dev split's balance. After review the record no longer uses the catalogue's general 'succeeded', which is untagged functional (a person can succeed several people in different offices), so the related-near inverse question rested only on a presupposition in the notes. Papal succession is one-to-one in both directions (each pope has one immediate predecessor and one immediate successor), so the new relation carries functional on both rows, each with a relation check. Related near asks the inverse (who came after John Paul II). Its original answer comes from the stored 'Benedict XVI succeeded John Paul II', a fact about another pope that the edit does not name; with preceded_as_pope functional, holding it next to the edit is inconsistent (John Paul II would have two immediate successors), so by step 3 of the determinacy procedure that route is dropped and the question has the single answer Pope Francis. Related far binds the subject through his birth name, Jorge Mario Bergoglio, which every model holds as a separate fact and under which the 2013 succession was widely reported. Derived: two compositions on the new value (John Paul II's country, his birth name) and a binding through 'the first pope from the Americas'. The edit skips Benedict XVI; it need not be plausible. Counts are exact-phrase Dolma counts unless marked approximate.
